t: Raised in Muhammad's household, Ali was among the first to accept Islam, married Muhammad's daughter Fatima and served as his secretary, deputy and standard-bearer in Medina.
After Muhammad's death in 632 Sunni and Shia Muslims tell the succession differently: Sunnis accept Abu Bakr's appointment, while Shia Muslims hold that Muhammad had designated Ali at Ghadir Khumm.

Ali became caliph in 656 after Uthman's assassination, fought civil wars against Aisha, Talha, Zubayr and Mu'awiya, and was murdered in Kufa in 661, after which Mu'awiya founded the Umayyad Caliphate.
dyk: Ali's own father, Abu Talib, raised Muhammad, and Ali later came under Muhammad's guardianship when he was about five years old.
ev: Ali is born in Mecca to Abu Talib and Fatima bint Asad
He stays in Muhammad's bed as a decoy on the night Muhammad leaves for Medina
At Ghadir Khumm Muhammad says, "He whose mawla I am, Ali is his mawla"
The electoral council chooses Uthman over Ali
Ali takes the oath as caliph and wins the Battle of the Camel
The Battle of Siffin against Mu'awiya ends in a call for arbitration
He defeats the Kharijites at the Battle of Nahrawan and loses Egypt
He is assassinated at Kufa and Mu'awiya later founds the Umayyad Caliphate

f.born: c. 600 in Mecca, son of Abu Talib ibn Abd al-Muttalib and Fatima bint Asad, of the Banu Hashim clan of the Quraysh
f.died: c. 28 January 661 (19 Ramadan 40 AH) at the Great Mosque of Kufa, struck during the morning prayer by the Kharijite Ibn Muljam; other given dates are 26 and 30 January, and he died of his wounds about two days later
f.role: Fourth Rashidun caliph, 656 to 661; for Sunni Muslims the last of the rightly guided caliphs, for Shia Muslims the first Imam and the designated successor of Muhammad
f.known: early support of Muhammad; marriage to Fatima; Ghadir Khumm; the Battle of the Camel; the Battle of Siffin; the Kharijites; Nahj al-balagha
